conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy -- -D warnings (issue specifies cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings); workspace lints in root Cargo.toml: unreachable_pub = warn, undocumented_unsafe_blocks/unwrap_used/expect_used = deny, must_use_candidate = warn; cargo deny check advisories licenses bans; jscpd duplication report is advisory; SPDX two-line header required on new .rs files (CONTRIBUTING.md).
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option or Vec and never panic (java.rs and swift.rs extract_inheritance); get_node_text in languages/mod.rs does a bounds check and returns Option<String> (used by swift.rs); lookup failures surface as ParserError::UnsupportedLanguage (parser.rs 221-226) or AnalyzeError::UnsupportedLanguage (analyze.rs 39-40, 495); no .unwrap() or .expect() in production code.

patterns: Registry pattern: handler module with pub const query strings and optional fn handlers, then one match arm in get_language_info() and one in get_ts_language(), plus a row in EXTENSION_MAP and an entry in supported_languages() (lang.rs).

Five-constant handler shape: ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY (java.rs, swift.rs, kotlin.rs, csharp.rs all follow it; fortran.rs and markdown.rs set defuse_query: None).

Java-style inheritance uses child_by_field_name("superclass") and child_by_field_name("interfaces") (java.rs); PHP has no such fields, so the Java walk does not transfer and the Swift child-scan style is the right template.
Swift-style inheritance scans node.child(i) for the clause kind, takes named_child(0) and calls get_node_text, and emits prefixed strings ('extends X' / 'conforms Y') (swift.rs 49-75).

Element capture contract: @function / @class outer captures with func_name|method_name and class_name|type_name inner captures (parser_elements.rs 285-296); a missing inner capture falls back to child_by_field_name("name") for classes.

extract_inheritance is invoked for every @class capture, so interface, trait and enum nodes also reach the handler (parser_elements.rs 398-410). The PHP handler must therefore handle base_clause (extends) on interfaces as well as class_interface_clause (implements) on classes and enums.
Defuse capture prefixes classify sites: write. -> Write, read. -> Read, writeread. -> WriteRead; reads at the same byte offset as a write are dropped (parser_elements.rs 850-895).

Import capture fallback: any import node kind not matched by name is stored as its full source text in ImportInfo.module with empty items (parser_elements.rs 146-156), so (namespace_use_declaration) @import_path needs no parser change.
enclosing_function_name already recognises function_definition and method_declaration by the name field (parser_elements.rs 440-446), so call-site caller attribution works for PHP without changes.
CSS handler ships CALL_QUERY as an empty string and defuse_query None (mod.rs 264-279); a language with no call sites uses this shape.

constraints: Maintainers implement #1864 in-house; the issue states external pull requests will be closed, so the work is internal-only.

Scope is fixed by the issue: new php.rs, registry wiring in languages/mod.rs and lang.rs, Cargo entries, unit tests in php.rs, one integration test file under crates/aptu-coder/tests/, README update. Tool handler and schema changes are out of scope.

Excluded extensions: .phtml, .inc, .module, .php5. Excluded functions: extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type. Excluded features: trait use resolution, property and constant extraction, attributes, namespace alias imports.

Dependency gate: new Cargo.lock entries must be at least 7 days old (AGENTS.md); the issue forbids SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK for this crate. tree-sitter-php v0.25.2 GitHub release is dated 2026-11-19T16:26:36Z, which is 8 days before this run; the crates.io publish time could not be checked from this environment.
Licensing: tree-sitter-php is MIT (Cargo.toml in the grammar repo); deny.toml's license allow-list includes MIT.
Grammar ABI: workspace tree-sitter is 0.27.1 (Cargo.lock 0.27.2); tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 dev-depends on tree-sitter 0.27, so the runtime and grammar versions are compatible.

Language must be in supported_languages(): parser.rs get_compiled_queries (221-226) looks up QUERY_CACHE, which is built from supported_languages() (191-196). A get_language_info() arm alone is not enough.

Use LANGUAGE_PHP (mixed HTML/PHP dialect), not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, because the issue requires a file with HTML outside <?php ?> to parse with zero ERROR nodes; the php_only program rule has no text rule (define-grammar.js lines 166-179 branch on dialect).
Workspace lints deny unwrap_used and expect_used in production code; the test-code exemption is set in each crate's lib.rs (AGENTS.md).
Every new .rs file needs the two-line SPDX header (CONTRIBUTING.md).
Clone state: an untracked .exp5-fence/ directory exists at the clone root; it was not read or modified.
test_coverage: No PHP coverage exists (no 'php' in EXTENSION_MAP, no languages/php.rs, no tree-sitter-php in Cargo.lock). Affected areas and their current tests: (1) languages/*.rs inline tests cover query compilation, element matching, inheritance and defuse for java.rs, swift.rs and kotlin.rs, and CSS query and empty-file cases in css.rs; (2) languages/mod.rs test_get_language_info_covers_remaining_registered_languages (383-412) asserts reference/import presence per registered language, and a PHP row would be added there; (3) lang.rs tests (102+) cover language_for_extension happy and edge cases and the schema pattern test that iterates supported_extensions(), so a 'php' row is exercised automatically; (4) core integration_tests.rs test_integration_tsx_analyze_file (3139) shows the end-to-end analyze_file pattern to copy; (5) crates/aptu-coder/tests has no language-specific file-type integration test beyond the shared harness. Gap: nothing currently proves a mixed HTML/PHP file yields zero ERROR nodes, and nothing exercises DEFUSE_QUERY for a dynamic language with no local declaration statement.

approaches.name: A: Full five-query handler mirroring java.rs and swift.rs, using LANGUAGE_PHP (recommended)
approaches.description: Add languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration) and DEFUSE_QUERY (assignment, augmented assignment, update, static/global/parameter declarations, variable reads). Add extract_inheritance that walks named children of class-like nodes: base_clause gives 'extends X', class_interface_clause gives 'implements X'. Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP. Wire 'php' in get_language_info, get_ts_language, the table test, EXTENSION_MAP ('php','php') and supported_languages(). Add tree-sitter-php to root and core Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock.
pros: Matches every acceptance criterion in #1864, including the mixed HTML/PHP parse with zero ERROR nodes (LANGUAGE_PHP handles text outside php tags).

No parser.rs or parser_elements.rs change: all capture names (function, class, func_name, method_name, class_name, call, import_path, type_ref, write.*, read.*, writeread.*) already fit the dispatch code.
enclosing_function_name, import fallback and the defuse dedup logic already handle the PHP node kinds.
Same shape as the most recent language addition (Swift, #1742), so review is mechanical.
cons: PHP has no local_variable_declaration analog. The Java write.local pattern is replaced by write.assign plus write.local on static_variable_declaration, global_declaration and simple_parameter, so def-use semantics differ from Java.
Variables are captured as the bare name without '$' (variable_name > name), so a symbol lookup for '$x' must strip the sigil. This is a behaviour decision the tests must pin.
Adding 'php' to supported_languages() is an easy-to-miss step; without it the lookup fails at parser.rs 221-226 even though get_language_info returns Some.
tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 age-gate margin is thin (see constraints); may need a version fallback.
Largest diff of the three options (about 8 files and about 600 lines including tests).

approaches.name: B: Pure-PHP grammar (LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) with the same handler
approaches.description: Identical php.rs and registry wiring to A, but register tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY instead of LANGUAGE_PHP. The php_only dialect's program rule is optional(php_tag), repeat(statement), optional(php_end_tag) in define-grammar.js, with no text rule, so HTML outside the tags is not a valid statement.
pros: Smaller grammar surface for pure .php files; no text or php_end_tag handling in the query paths.
Same handler code as A, so the query text and tests carry over.
cons: Fails the issue's acceptance criterion for a mixed HTML/PHP file: HTML text outside <?php ?> is expected to produce ERROR nodes under this dialect.
Silently wrong for template files, which are common in PHP codebases.
Would need a second grammar entry per dialect or a per-file dispatch, which expands wiring and Cargo entries beyond the issue's scope.

approaches.name: C: Ship without DEFUSE_QUERY (defuse_query: None), like fortran.rs
approaches.description: Implement ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY and extract_inheritance, set defuse_query: None in get_language_info, and omit the DEFUSE_QUERY constant. Everything else as in A.
pros: Removes the most PHP-specific judgement call (write/read semantics for a language with no local declaration statement).
Smaller test surface: no defuse tests needed; fewer lines to review.
Precedent exists: fortran.rs has defuse_query: None in mod.rs.
cons: Violates the issue's Scope and Acceptance Criteria, which require the five query constants and DEFUSE_QUERY in php.rs. The DEFUSE_QUERY constant is required because the issue lists it explicitly, and because every OO handler in the registry (java, kotlin, csharp, swift, python, typescript) sets defuse_query to Some.
Symbol-level def-use queries for PHP return nothing; that is a functional gap for the analyze tools that consume DefUse sites.
Needs a follow-up issue to add defuse later, which is more churn than doing it once.

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets every stated acceptance criterion in #1864 and it reuses the existing capture contract, so no parser change is needed. Use LANGUAGE_PHP, not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, because the mixed HTML/PHP criterion requires it. Implement extract_inheritance with a named-child walk over base_clause and class_interface_clause, not Java's child_by_field_name. Add 'php' to supported_languages() as well as EXTENSION_MAP and the two match arms, since missing the list fails at lookup. Before merging, confirm the tree-sitter-php crates.io publish date (0.25.2 vs 0.25.1) against the 7-day gate, and compile all five queries in a unit test as the issue suggests. Note: this run could not compile the queries (no build executed, read-only constraint); the query text is derived from node-types.json and define-grammar.js and is unverified until Query::new runs.

inheritance_walk_citation:
Grammar source: tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php, php/grammar.js (3 lines, calls defineGrammar('php')) and common/define-grammar.js (1738 lines), inspected in Step 4; php/src/node-types.json confirms the fields.
1. class_declaration (define-grammar.js lines 365-373): optional(field('attributes', attribute_list)), repeat(_modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list). The extends and implements clauses carry no field name.
2. base_clause (lines 334-337): keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name). node-types.json lists base_clause children: name, qualified_name, relative_name.
3. class_interface_clause (lines 381-384): keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name). node-types.json lists the same three children.
4. _name (define-grammar.js) is choice(alias(keyword static), alias(cast type names), reserved('classes', name), qualified_name, relative_name), so a base name is a name node or a qualified_name node.
5. node-types.json fields for class_declaration: attributes, body, name only; children include base_clause and class_interface_clause. There is no 'superclass' or 'interfaces' field, so Java's child_by_field_name walk does not apply.
6. Walk to implement: for each named child c of the class node, if c.kind() == 'base_clause' then for each named child n of c with kind name, qualified_name or relative_name emit 'extends ' + text(n); if c.kind() == 'class_interface_clause' then emit 'implements ' + text(n) for each such n. Use named_children(&mut cursor) (Context7-confirmed tree-sitter API) and get_node_text from languages/mod.rs for bounds-checked text.
7. interface_declaration (lines 326-332) also places base_clause as an unnamed child, so the same walk yields 'extends A' for each parent interface. enum_declaration (lines 339-347) places class_interface_clause as an unnamed child, so it yields 'implements X'. The parser calls extract_inheritance for every @class capture (parser_elements.rs 398-410), so the handler must accept all four node kinds.
